dispositions.rationale: Text unchanged since the merged record's round, where this lens read it without objection; on substance: BRF-A28 judges the skill text as S3.4's deliverable and F1 to F7 judge the writer's behaviour under BRF-A16 to BRF-A20; neither claims the other (merged record, behavioural-outcome-1).

Text unchanged since the merged record's round, where this lens read it without objection; on substance: every sentence of BRF-A9 is decided by the one grammar-fixture test family, and the counterpart markings are how each suite's fixture test finds the parser it checks; one observation, one obligation (brief5 round, behavioural-outcome-1).

Text unchanged since the merged record's round, where this lens read it without objection; on substance: one observation, two runs in one directory with outputs and directory compared, decides all three clauses of BRF-A30 (brief5 round, behavioural-outcome-3).

Repeats obligation-reduction-1 to -3 of the merged record: the evaluation claims fidelity over its seven fixtures under the stochastic rule, and the per-brief guard is check (BRF-A8, BRF-A23), which BRF-A28 makes the skill require before every dispatch; F3 to F5 sample the refusal sources.

Repeats obligation-reduction-1 to -3 of the merged record: the evaluation claims fidelity over its seven fixtures under the stochastic rule, and the per-brief guard is check (BRF-A8, BRF-A23), which BRF-A28 makes the skill require before every dispatch; F3 to F5 sample the refusal sources.

F6 samples the writer's judgment on one infeasible check, and judging feasibility in code is out of scope by the spec's own list; BRF-D5 now names the writer's judgment as an unready reason and BRF-D8 states the runs measure it, never prove it.

Artifact placement is what the installer and the slice list fix, and the installer stages the skill directory whole (merged record, obligation-reduction-5); a criterion observing a path proves no behaviour, which the acceptance-criteria standard forbids.

Repeats obligation-reduction-10 of the merged record: the helper is stdlib-only and its suite runs where no tracker storage exists; a second resolver is a code-review read.

Repeats obligation-reduction-11 of the merged record: content-lint measures every deployed skill body against its cap and fails the gate above it; a content-lint that skips the file is the gate's defect, not this spec's.

Repeats obligation-reduction-12 of the merged record: the attestation is the record; the tree cannot observe the execution it attests (BRF-D8). The configured model is now pinned in the scorer and the record must equal it (BRF-A26).
Repeats obligation-reduction-13 of the merged record: BRF-D8 states the repeat limit is an operator procedure because no output shows a retry.

Rests on the operator, as the merged record's obligation-reduction-14 states: nothing in the committed tree can observe a run, output, report or attempt that was never committed, nor a dispatch history.

The fingerprint excludes evals/, so a scorer change alters no fingerprint and BRF-A33 keeps every lock current or fallen on its stored runs; whether the operator dispatches writers anyway is an act the tree cannot observe.

Reading a failed run and judging it a defect is the operator's act. BRF-D8 states the response, changing the skill, which voids the lock, as procedure, and the scope excludes judging in code what only a reading decides.

The installer prunes every test file and every evals/ directory by its own .installignore, which the current-state section now records, and that staging check is the installer's gate, outside this spec's scope.

Text unchanged since the merged record's round, where this lens read it without objection; on substance: BRF-D3 defines fidelity as the set of IDs and their words read by the shared grammar, so a line outside an entry in a brief's criteria section is no entry, the brief's ID set differs from its source's, and check exits 1 under BRF-A8 naming the difference; the refusal codes are for sources, which a brief is not.

parts.statement: Actual dispatched briefs preserve the assigned contract across assignments, including cases outside the fixed evaluation fixtures.

obligations.source: Scope: "A dispatch brief must carry exactly the criteria assigned to the work." BRF-D3: "A changed word, a dropped or added ID, or a changed ID is a different contract."
obligations.statement: Every dispatched brief carries exactly its assigned criterion IDs and source words.

parts.statement: Actual dispatched briefs contain the complete, faithful evidence mapping across assignments.

obligations.source: Scope: "It must map each criterion to its planned check, apart from the criterion's text." BRF-D3: "An observation and a pass rule must therefore equal the planned ones."
obligations.statement: Every dispatched brief maps each criterion to its planned check separately from the criterion text.

parts.statement: Actual writer behavior relays every applicable refusal instead of dispatching a brief.

obligations.source: Scope: "It must refuse when it cannot." BRF-D4: "The skill tells the writer to relay a refusal to its requester and dispatch nothing."
obligations.statement: When the assigned contract cannot be supplied, the writer relays the refusal and dispatches nothing.

parts.statement: Actual writer behavior detects and reports infeasible checks, including infeasibility beyond absent or blank fields and F6's example.

obligations.source: Scope: "A criterion without a feasible planned check is reported unready." BRF-D5: "Whether a stated check is feasible is the writer's judgment" and "the skill tells the writer not to dispatch a brief with an unready criterion."
obligations.statement: A criterion without a feasible planned check is reported unready and prevents dispatch.

parts.statement: brief_criteria.py ships beside SKILL.md.
The shared grammar fixture lives in the skill's evals directory.
The mechanical scorer is delivered as evals/score_briefs.py.
The helper tests and spec-lint fixture test occupy the files specified by S3.1.

obligations.source: BRF-D1: "The skill ships brief_criteria.py beside its SKILL.md." BRF-D2: "It lives in the skill's evals/." BRF-D8: "evals/score_briefs.py scores the outputs mechanically." S3.1 names brief_criteria_test.py and packages/installer/tests/unit/test_spec_lint.py.
obligations.statement: The implementation delivers the artifacts at the locations specified by the design and slice list.

parts.statement: Spec-source emission contains exactly the assigned IDs and their full source text, including large assignments.
Criteria-file emission contains exactly the file's entries.
Item-source emission contains exactly the renderer's criteria.
Successful and unready emission contains criteria and evidence, contains no third section, and preserves the criteria section across checks configurations.

obligations.source: BRF-D1: "Its emit mode prints exactly two Markdown sections." BRF-D2 names spec, criteria-file and item sources. BRF-D5: "The criteria section is the same whether --checks is absent, complete or leaves a criterion unready."
obligations.statement: emit produces the assigned criteria and evidence as exactly two Markdown sections.

parts.statement: Entry recognition and text extraction honor entry syntax, section boundaries, continuation joining, terminators and fenced-code exclusions.

obligations.source: BRF-D2: "Spec and file entries follow spec-lint's entry grammar, joined text included" and the five numbered grammar rules.
obligations.statement: Source entries follow the specified five-rule grammar, with the heading restriction omitted for criteria files.

parts.statement: The fixture represents every grammar rule, both suites check expected readings, rule-breaking helper variants fail cases, counterpart markings exist, and fixture absence fails both suites.

obligations.source: BRF-D2: "each carries a marking naming the other"; "One fixture keeps the two readings from drifting apart unseen"; "both suites read it"; "Both suites fail when the fixture is absent."
obligations.statement: A shared fixture and counterpart markings expose drift between the helper parser and spec-lint.

parts.statement: emit and check refuse zero or multiple source flags and name the flags given.

obligations.source: BRF-D2: "Exactly one source flag is given. More than one, or none, refuses as source-conflict."
obligations.statement: Exactly one source flag is required.

parts.statement: Without checks, check accepts precisely preserved criteria and names every missing, added or altered ID on rejection.
With checks, check accepts preserved criteria and evidence and rejects missing, added or altered evidence, including changes to unready marks and reasons.

obligations.source: BRF-D3: "Its criteria section holds exactly the assigned IDs"; text equals source after whitespace collapse; "Order is not compared." Evidence follows the same rule against the plan.
obligations.statement: check compares criterion and evidence contracts using exact ID sets and whitespace-normalized source text, without imposing order.

parts.statement: Readable, well-formed empty assignments refuse as no-criteria, including empty rendered item criteria.
Absent assigned spec IDs refuse as unretrievable and name the IDs.
Missing or unreadable sources and briefs refuse as unreadable-source with the required path and assigned-ID details.
Repeated assigned or defined IDs refuse as duplicate-id and name the ID.
Nonblank criteria-file text outside entries refuses as malformed-criteria with line details, without also claiming no-criteria.
Malformed checks and failed item rendering produce their specified refusal codes and details.
check applies the same refusals as emit for shared failing sources.
Refusals use empty stdout, one stderr JSON object and exit 2, and aggregate every detectable readable-source fault.

obligations.source: BRF-D4: "emit prints nothing on stdout and one JSON object on stderr naming each fault, and exits 2"; the refusal-code list; "One refusal names every fault the helper detects in the sources it can read." BRF-D1 also defines check mode.
obligations.statement: Helper refusals use the specified codes, fault details, output channels and exit status, including aggregated faults.

parts.statement: Complete checks produce exactly the assigned evidence entries and exit 0; well-formed unassigned entries have no effect.
Missing entries, absent keys and whitespace-only fields produce the specified unready reasons, stderr IDs and exit 1; absent checks makes every criterion unready.
Every checks entry is shape-validated; missing keys are blank rather than malformed, and unrelated keys are ignored regardless of value.
Changes in checks completeness do not change the emitted criterion text.

obligations.source: BRF-D5 defines the checks JSON shape, blank fields, ignored keys and unassigned entries, the closed reason set, and emit's exit-1 behavior.
obligations.statement: The helper maps planned observations and pass rules to assigned IDs and distinguishes malformed plans from unready criteria.

parts.statement: emit and check require no importable third-party package and produce equivalent results under the two runtimes.

obligations.source: BRF-D1: "The helper uses the standard library only, so it runs under uv run or python3 on every supported tool."
obligations.statement: The helper runs with the standard library under python3 and uv run on supported tools.

parts.statement: The helper calls the renderer, emits its criteria and makes no other facade call.
The helper never independently resolves the item's acceptance field.
An unavailable render verb or rendering failure refuses as render-failed with the item and cause.

obligations.source: BRF-D7: "--item runs work acceptance render ID" and "It never resolves an item's acceptance field itself, since that would be a third resolver of LIFE-D1."
obligations.statement: Item criteria come exclusively from the facade renderer, without an independent acceptance-field resolver.

parts.statement: The acceptance-criteria text and skeleton contain all four required routing instructions.
The rewritten skill complies with the applicable token caps.

obligations.source: BRF-D6: "Criteria and evidence come from emit, pasted unchanged, and check runs before dispatch. A refusal or an unready criterion is reported to the requester." "Content-lint's token caps apply."
obligations.statement: The rewritten skill and skeleton prescribe the helper route and comply with content-lint's token caps.

parts.statement: Actual runs use the prescribed model and execution route, fresh contexts, source-tree skill, fixed tasks and tool restriction; model changes amend the spec.
Records contain the configured model identity, fingerprint and required operator attestations.

obligations.source: BRF-D8: "The writer is a Claude Opus model through the native Agent tool"; source-tree skill by full path; configured model held constant; fixed tasks; fresh contexts; no subagent tool; record names the resolved model and attests fresh contexts and native Agent use.
obligations.statement: Evaluation execution follows the prescribed writer, model, context, tool and task protocol, and records its identity and attestations.

parts.statement: F1 and F2 meet the evaluation's preservation threshold.
F1 and F2 meet the evaluation's evidence-mapping threshold.
F3 meets its report-and-no-criteria-refusal threshold.
F4 and F5 meet their report-and-detailed-refusal thresholds.
F6 and F7 meet their report-and-unready-ID thresholds.

obligations.source: BRF-D8's F1–F7 table and locking rule. S3.5 requires "the committed attempts that lock every fixture."
obligations.statement: The evaluation of record locks all seven fixed fixtures using their prescribed observations and thresholds.

parts.statement: The prescribed refusal and unready evaluations require valid report content.
The scorer rejects the seeded altered-content, invalid-report, missing-form and invalid-brief cases and locks all-five-passing sets.

obligations.source: BRF-D8 defines brief and report forms, requires Form lines, excludes criteria and evidence sections from reports, requires refusal relay and unready IDs, and scores preservation and evidence separately.
obligations.statement: The scorer mechanically distinguishes passing outputs from the specified invalid output forms and contents.

parts.statement: All-five-passing sides lock and the prescribed three-failure seeded sides fail.
A single intermediate side with every other side passing awaits its second five and then uses the eight-of-ten threshold.
The same side rules and fixture aggregation work when multiple sides simultaneously have intermediate or otherwise mixed states.

obligations.source: BRF-D8: five passes passes; three or four earns a second five; at least eight of ten passes; two or fewer fails; "A fixture is locked when every side passes."
obligations.statement: Every side follows the five-run and second-five rule, and fixtures lock only when every side passes.

parts.statement: Missing first-five outputs and required record fields prevent locking and produce incomplete rather than failed results.
The operator repeats only no-output runs and never repeats a run more than twice.

obligations.source: BRF-D8: "A run with no output is repeated at most twice. It is then left pending and never scored as failed." "A repeat is dispatched only for a run that has produced no output."
obligations.statement: Missing outputs leave evaluations pending, and repeats follow the bounded no-output-only procedure.

parts.statement: The scorer enforces counting cardinality and directory accounting, and excludes recorded superseded late outputs from scoring.
Each output itself names its run.
Missing named output files make the attempt incomplete.

obligations.source: BRF-D8: "Each output names its run"; the record names one counting output per run; late outputs are marked superseded; excessive or unaccounted outputs cause refusal.
obligations.statement: Outputs and records identify runs and account for every counting or superseded output.

parts.statement: Actual attempts, reports, all retained outputs, superseded late outputs and earned second fives are committed at the prescribed locations.

obligations.source: BRF-D8: "An attempt is committed under evals/runs/<run-id>/ with its outputs, its record and its report, whatever it shows, and a second five is committed beside the attempt it extends." Late outputs "stay committed."
obligations.statement: Evaluation evidence is committed and retained regardless of outcome.

parts.statement: The scorer computes the specified fingerprints, excludes mismatching or fallen locks, and retains matching locks whose stored runs still pass.
Only fixtures with changed fingerprints receive writer reruns; scorer-only changes rescore stored outputs without writer dispatch.

obligations.source: BRF-D8 defines fingerprint inputs and currentness; "A change voids only the locks whose fingerprint it alters, and only those fixtures run again." "A change to the scorer dispatches no writer."
obligations.statement: Fingerprints and rescoring govern lock currentness and restrict writer reruns to changed fixture fingerprints.

parts.statement: The scorer refuses later committed attempts with the same fingerprint regardless of the earlier outcome.

obligations.source: BRF-D8: "A fingerprint gets one attempt"; incomplete attempts are completed in place; the scorer refuses a second attempt for an already seen fingerprint.
obligations.statement: A fingerprint receives only one committed attempt, including when its attempt fails or remains incomplete.

parts.statement: Failed runs behind locks are read, and demonstrated defects cause skill correction followed by renewed evaluation.

obligations.source: BRF-D8: "A failed run behind a lock is committed and read like any other, and a defect it shows is answered by changing the skill, which voids the lock and runs the fixture again."
obligations.statement: Failures behind passing locks remain subject to inspection and defect correction.

parts.statement: Completion requires current locks for all prescribed generated-brief evaluation cases rather than helper checks alone.

obligations.source: Scope: "That boundary is the generated brief itself." BRF-D9: "The helper suites establish the mechanism. Only the evaluation of record establishes the parents at the generated brief."
obligations.statement: Verification establishes the parent outcomes at the generated-brief boundary through the evaluation of record.

parts.statement: content-tests executes the helper and scorer suites, ci executes the spec-lint fixture test, and seeded suite failures make their gates fail.

obligations.source: The S3.1 continuation names make content-tests and make ci; S3.2 and S3.3 name make content-tests. BRF-D9 assigns mechanism verification to the helper suites.
obligations.statement: The verification suites participate in the gates named by the slice continuations.

parts.statement: emit and check write no files, unchanged runs reproduce their outputs and status, and concurrent runs over different sources share nothing.

obligations.source: What-if questions: "emit and check read and never write"; repeated unchanged runs print the same result; "concurrent runs share nothing." BRF-D8 prescribes mechanical scoring.
obligations.statement: Helper runs are read-only, repeatable and isolated across concurrent sources.

parts.statement: Installation removes evals directories and all test files from deployed artifacts.

obligations.source: BRF-D2: "The installer prunes every test file along with evals/, so neither suite ever runs in a deployed tree, and nothing needs a skip."
obligations.statement: The deployed tree excludes evaluation directories and test files.

ground.reason: BRF-D6 promises that the writer takes sections from emit and runs check before dispatch. BRF-A28 verifies only that the skill text contains those instructions. The traceability row for 'the writer’s route' names only a content test. That test cannot establish that the writer follows the route.

objections.objection: The content test can accept a skill whose writer dispatches without running check.
objections.obligation: The writer runs check before dispatch, as required by BRF-D6.

scenario.expect: The content test passes because all four instructions appear, while the writer dispatches without the required check.
scenario.given: A skill containing all four BRF-A28 instructions, whose writer manually copies a faithful brief and skips check.
scenario.when: BRF-A28’s content test reads the skill text.

ground.reason: BRF-D2 requires both executable protection against grammar drift and parser markings naming their counterparts. BRF-A9 combines those obligations. Fixture conformance and rule-breaking variants can be delivered and accepted independently of the counterpart markings.

objections.objection: BRF-A9 combines grammar verification and parser discoverability in one acceptance decision.
objections.obligation: Shared grammar verification and counterpart markings.

scenario.expect: BRF-A9 passes as a whole, while no separate acceptance result distinguishes grammar verification from counterpart markings.
scenario.given: A deliverable with the shared fixture, passing conformance checks, failing rule-breaking variants, counterpart markings and missing-fixture failures.
scenario.when: BRF-A9 is assessed as one criterion.

ground.reason: BRF-A30 combines reproducible output, absence of file writes and isolation between concurrent runs. The What-if questions also name these guarantees. Each can hold or fail independently: deterministic output does not establish that no file is written, and neither establishes concurrency isolation.

objections.objection: BRF-A30 combines three independently acceptable guarantees in one criterion.
objections.obligation: Determinism, absence of file writes and concurrency isolation.

scenario.expect: BRF-A30 passes as a whole, while no separate acceptance result identifies which guarantee has been established independently.
scenario.given: A deliverable that produces identical repeated outputs, writes no files and isolates concurrent runs.
scenario.when: BRF-A30 is assessed as one criterion.

ground.reason: BRF-A16 observes thresholded runs on F1 and F2. It does not establish fidelity for other assignments or exclude fidelity failures among the runs behind a lock.

objections.objection: The criteria permit a writer to dispatch a brief with omitted, added or reworded criteria.

scenario.expect: Every criterion's check passes, but the dispatched brief omits one assigned criterion.
scenario.given: All seven fixtures hold current locks, the helper behaves correctly, and the skill contains the required instructions.
scenario.when: The writer briefs a different task with four assigned criteria and dispatches without following the instruction to run check.

ground.reason: BRF-A17 establishes evidence preservation at the declared threshold for F1 and F2. The helper checks and the skill's instruction text do not establish the evidence in every generated brief.

objections.objection: The criteria permit a dispatched brief whose evidence does not map every assigned criterion to its planned check.

scenario.expect: Every criterion's check passes, but one criterion has no evidence entry in the dispatched brief.
scenario.given: The helper and scorer pass their checks, and all fixed fixtures hold current locks.
scenario.when: The writer produces a brief for an assignment outside F1 and F2 and omits an evidence entry.

ground.reason: The refusal evaluations sample no assignment, one absent ID and an unreadable spec. They do not establish the writer's refusal behavior for every helper refusal, and their thresholds permit failed runs.

objections.objection: Correct helper refusals and passing evaluations can coexist with the writer dispatching an invented contract.

scenario.expect: Every criterion's check passes, but the writer dispatches a brief instead of relaying the refusal.
scenario.given: All fixed fixtures hold current locks and the helper correctly aggregates faults.
scenario.when: A different assignment contains two absent IDs, emit refuses naming both, and the writer invents their criteria and dispatches.

ground.reason: BRF-A11 checks missing or blank fields. BRF-A20 samples F6's subjective pass rule and F7's missing or blank fields. Neither discharges infeasibility outside those cases.

objections.objection: A nonblank but infeasible planned check can be treated as ready and dispatched.

scenario.expect: Every criterion's check passes, but the writer dispatches without reporting the criterion unready.
scenario.given: All fixed fixtures hold current locks. A new criterion has nonblank observation and pass strings requiring access to a service the writer cannot access.
scenario.when: The writer accepts the syntactically complete check as feasible.

ground.reason: The helper criteria observe its behavior, not whether it ships beside SKILL.md.

objections.objection: The helper can pass all checks while missing its promised deployment location.

scenario.expect: Every criterion's check passes, but brief_criteria.py is absent beside the skill.
scenario.given: A working helper resides elsewhere and the test harness invokes it there.
scenario.when: The implementation is accepted using its behavioral checks.

ground.reason: BRF-A9 checks the shared fixture's contents, use and absence handling. It does not check its location in the skill's evals directory.

objections.objection: The shared grammar fixture can satisfy its checks while violating the declared layout.

scenario.expect: Every criterion's check passes, but the grammar fixture is outside the skill's evals directory.
scenario.given: Both suites read a shared fixture stored in another repository directory.
scenario.when: The fixture, parser variants and absence tests are checked.

ground.reason: The scorer criteria observe scoring behavior, not the required evals/score_briefs.py artifact.

objections.objection: A scorer at another location can satisfy every scoring check.

scenario.expect: Every criterion's check passes, but evals/score_briefs.py is absent.
scenario.given: The scorer is implemented elsewhere and the suites and evaluation invoke that implementation.
scenario.when: All scorer and generated-brief checks run.

ground.reason: BRF-A9 and BRF-A31 establish fixture use and gate participation, not the test files named by the slice plan.

objections.objection: The test implementation can pass its checks without the declared test artifacts.

scenario.expect: Every criterion's check passes, but brief_criteria_test.py and the fixture test in the named installer test file are absent.
scenario.given: Equivalent tests live in other files and their gates execute them.
scenario.when: The helper, fixture and gate checks run.

ground.reason: BRF-A13 checks rendered output and facade calls. It does not observe whether the helper independently resolves an item's acceptance field.

objections.objection: A third acceptance-field resolver can coexist with the required renderer call and output.

scenario.expect: Every criterion's check passes, but the helper resolves the acceptance field itself.
scenario.given: The helper calls acceptance render and also reads and resolves the item's acceptance field directly, without another facade call.
scenario.when: The stub-facade checks run and emit returns exactly the rendered criteria.

ground.reason: BRF-A28 checks four instructions in the skill text. A content-lint exit status observes the gate result; no criterion observes compliance with the token caps.

objections.objection: The skill can contain every required instruction while exceeding the applicable token caps.

scenario.expect: Every criterion's check passes, but the skill exceeds its token cap.
scenario.given: The skill contains the four required instructions and excessive additional text. The content-lint invocation skips that file.
scenario.when: The content test and continuation's content-lint gate run successfully.

ground.reason: BRF-A26 checks recorded model identity and attestations. Those artifact properties do not establish the execution conditions they describe or pin the configured writer to the promised model.

objections.objection: Passing records can represent evaluations conducted with a different model, reused contexts or a different execution route.

scenario.expect: Every criterion's check passes, but the actual writer runs violate the prescribed execution protocol.
scenario.given: The stored outputs pass all scoring rules and the record names the configured model and carries the required attestations.
scenario.when: Those outputs are produced through a CLI in reused contexts rather than by the prescribed Claude Opus writer through the native Agent tool.

ground.reason: BRF-A32 exercises one side at three or four passes while every other side passes. BRF-A27 exercises seeded failures and all-five success. Neither covers simultaneous intermediate states on F1's or F2's two sides.

objections.objection: The scorer can mishandle a fixture whose preservation and evidence sides both earn a second five.

scenario.expect: Every criterion's check passes, but the scorer fails the fixture immediately instead of awaiting its second five.
scenario.given: A complete F1 attempt has three passing preservation runs and four passing evidence runs among its first five outputs.
scenario.when: The scorer encounters both intermediate sides together, a combination absent from the prescribed scorer checks.

ground.reason: BRF-A26 observes missing outputs and incomplete records. No criterion observes dispatch history, the repeat limit or whether a repeated run previously produced output.

objections.objection: An evaluation can obtain its counting outputs through prohibited repeats.

scenario.expect: Every criterion's check passes, but a run has been repeated three times.
scenario.given: A run produces no output on its original dispatch and its first two repeats.
scenario.when: The operator dispatches a third repeat, obtains a passing output and records it among the fixture's five counting outputs.

ground.reason: BRF-A35 checks the record's counting and supersession relationships. It does not check that each output names its own run.

objections.objection: Outputs without run identities can be counted under an otherwise valid record.

scenario.expect: Every criterion's check passes, but the output does not name its run.
scenario.given: Each output has the required Form line and passing content, and the record assigns exactly one existing output to each run.
scenario.when: The scorer counts an output whose body contains no run identity.

ground.reason: The criteria inspect records, directories and lock calculations. They do not establish that actual attempts, reports, second fives and superseded outputs are committed.

objections.objection: The evaluation can pass while its required evidence remains uncommitted.

scenario.expect: Every criterion's check passes, but the evaluation evidence is not committed under evals/runs/<run-id>/.
scenario.given: The scorer's committed-input tests pass, and actual evaluation files contain valid records, outputs, reports and current locks.
scenario.when: The actual evaluation is scored from untracked files and accepted without committing them.

ground.reason: BRF-A33 checks lock currentness and rescoring results. It does not observe which writer dispatches occur after a change.

objections.objection: Correct lock calculations can coexist with prohibited writer reruns.

scenario.expect: Every criterion's check passes, but a scorer-only change dispatches writers.
scenario.given: Existing fingerprints still match and stored outputs still pass under an amended scorer.
scenario.when: The operator launches fresh writer runs, leaves them outside the recorded attempts, and then correctly rescores and retains the existing locks.

ground.reason: The locking criteria permit passing thresholds with failed runs. No criterion observes whether those runs are read or whether a demonstrated defect is answered by changing the skill.

objections.objection: A lock can be accepted while a defect shown by a failed run remains unexamined and unfixed.

scenario.expect: Every criterion's check passes, but the failed run is never read and its demonstrated skill defect remains.
scenario.given: A side locks at eight passing runs out of ten. A retained failed run demonstrates that the writer drops an assigned criterion.
scenario.when: The operator accepts the lock without reading that run or changing the skill to address the defect.

ground.reason: No criterion observes the deployed tree or the installer's removal of test files.

objections.objection: All source-tree checks can pass while test files ship with the skill.

scenario.expect: Every criterion's check passes, but the deployed skill contains a test file.
scenario.given: All helper, scorer, fixture, content and evaluation checks pass in the repository.
scenario.when: The installer prunes evals but copies brief_criteria_test.py into the deployed skill directory.

ground.reason: BRF-D5 declares the unready reasons a closed set (no planned check, blank observation, blank pass rule) and states feasibility judgment is the writer's, yet BRF-D8's report definition and BRF-A20 require the writer to name an ID 'unready under BRF-D5' precisely for a check the closed set cannot mark. The wording leaves open whether an infeasible-but-present planned check can be reported unready at all.

objections.objection: F6's pass condition is unreachable under one reading and reachable under another: under the closed-set reading the helper exits 0 with no unready mark, so the writer has no defined basis to name the ID unready and must dispatch a brief, failing every F6 run; under the feasibility reading the writer reports the ID and the fixture can pass.

scenario.expect: Under the closed-set reading of BRF-D5 the writer dispatches a brief and the run fails BRF-A20; under the feasibility reading the writer returns a report naming the ID and the run passes. The same circumstance yields opposite verdicts.
